key_findings.finding: Direct experimental evidence answers yes: aliskiren inhibited prorenin-induced migration in cultured human aortic smooth muscle cells. In the study, cells were incubated with angiotensinogen (1.5×10⁻⁷ M) and aliskiren (10⁻⁶–10⁻⁵ M) for 24 h, then migration was tested in a Boyden chamber with prorenin (10⁻⁸ M) as chemoattractant. At 10⁻⁵ M, aliskiren reduced prorenin-induced migration by 66.4±18.1% (p<0.05); no significant inhibition occurred with PDGF-BB-driven migration. PMID 25070349, “Aliskiren inhibits prorenin-induced human aortic smooth muscle cell migration” (2015).

source_tools.relevance: Direct study result and experimental conditions in abstract

key_findings.finding: Mechanistic context: the earlier HASMC study found prorenin is chemotactic through the (pro)renin receptor; PRR knockdown completely abolished prorenin-induced migration, while Rac1 or RhoA suppression also blocked the response. This supports PRR-mediated prorenin migration as the experimental context for the aliskiren follow-up, but does not itself test aliskiren.
